$schema_note: Spec for a Court of Beasts wager dice graphic. Today the die is only an emoji (🎲) plus the rolled number in the wager-result banner; this describes a real graphic you could drop in to replace it. Two-layer convention: supply the art, Claude Code wires it in.

where_it_appears.context: The wager-result banner shown when an online friend match ends and both players wagered.
where_it_appears.current_markup: 🎲 {roll} inside the banner's label line, above the forfeited/won card image.
where_it_appears.sits_above: the card image (min(34vw, 150px) wide, gold-bordered), which shows which creature changed hands

what_the_graphic_represents: The result of the loser's six-sided roll (1-6) that decides which card is forfeited: 1-5 = the fielded card at that position (left to right), 6 = a random drafted-but-unpicked card.

canvas.generate_at: 512x512 per face (or a single 1536x1024 sheet of all six)
canvas.displayed_at: 48-72px in the banner (so keep pips/numerals bold and readable when small)

A_static_faces.desc: Six face images (values 1-6). Claude Code shows the one matching the roll, with a quick pop/settle animation via CSS.
A_static_faces.deliver: 6 square PNGs (die-1.png … die-6.png) with transparent background, OR one horizontal sheet of 6 faces evenly spaced.

B_animated_roll.desc: A short tumble that settles on the rolled value. More drama, more work to wire.
B_animated_roll.deliver: either a 6-frame-per-value sprite, a looping-then-settling MP4/WebM (~1s, transparent or on the banner's dark ground), or a CSS/SVG 3D cube Claude Code builds from six face images.
B_animated_roll.note: If you want this, the six faces from approach A are still the raw material.

face_design.style: Matches the coins and title plaque: a carved/cast object, top-lit, gold + dark stone, not a flat cartoon die.
options: Pips (classic 1-6 dot layout) carved as gem insets or gold studs on a dark stone/bone die
Roman numerals (I-VI) stamped like the coin emblems
Arabic numerals (1-6) in the same beveled cast-gold as the title lettering
face_design.recommendation: Pips as gems/studs read fastest at 48-72px and feel the most 'die'; numerals also fine and more legible.
face_design.body: aged bone-white or dark arcane stone cube face with a subtle bevel and worn edges; a thin gold rim optional

palette.pip_or_numeral: gold #d79425 or gem-inset (sapphire for the player, but a neutral gold is safest since either side can roll)

lighting: single warm light from above; specular glints on pips/edges; soft occlusion where pips meet the face — same treatment as the coin emblems.

delivery.background: transparent PNG (the banner ground is dark #08060e); a plain-black background also works since it's masked/dropped like the coins were
delivery.safe_area: keep pips/numerals inside the central ~80% so a rounded-corner or circular crop never clips them
delivery.naming: die-1.png … die-6.png (approach A), or dice-sheet.png (6 faces left-to-right), or dice-roll.webm (approach B)

notes_for_wiring: The roll value is already computed in App.tsx; wiring the graphic means swapping the 🎲 {roll} for an of the matching face (approach A) or a short clip (approach B).
The die shows on BOTH players' screens (winner and loser) with the same value, so a single neutral-colored die is correct — don't tint it per player.
